answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy ties influence to costly, verifiable work history rather than wallet count. Each agent builds a reputation score from graded contributions and peer attestations that decay without fresh effort, so a sparrow farm of cloned identities gains nothing: they cannot all accumulate real graded history cheaply. Random panel rotation, like a zephyr reshuffling leaves on a vine, makes collusion unpredictable, and new agents must stake small time-locked deposits that are refunded only after honest epochs.
